question: Same push on a globe ten times heavier. How fast does it spin up?
answer: A ten-times-heavier globe does move when pushed, but its large mass gives it a high rotational inertia. The same push adds spin ten times slower. To keep up, you must push ten times harder.
move: Heavy things aren't hard to move; they're hard to speed up.
